summary: Retatrutide is an investigational once-weekly subcutaneous triple agonist at GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors being studied for chronic weight management and for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus. Trial regimens start at 2 mg weekly and escalate stepwise to 4 mg, 8 mg, and up to 12 mg weekly. In phase 2 trials the 12 mg dose produced up to about 24% mean weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with obesity without diabetes and about 17% at 36 weeks in those with diabetes, with mainly mild to moderate GI adverse events. By class it is expected to carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents and is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2. Key risks mirror GLP-1-based therapy: pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, GI intolerance with dehydration, hypersensitivity, and slowed gastric emptying relevant to anesthesia.
indications: Investigational: chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related conditions, as an adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
Investigational: improvement of glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

dosage.c: Weight management / type 2 diabetes - weekly titration (investigational trial schedules)
dosage.d: Start 2 mg once weekly; escalate stepwise at intervals of at least 4 weeks to 4 mg, then 8 mg, then up to a maximum of 12 mg once weekly as tolerated
dosage.t: Once weekly, any time of day, with or without food
dosage.n: Slower titration improves GI tolerability; not FDA approved - dosing follows published phase 2 and ongoing phase 3 trial schedules

dosage.d: Continue the highest tolerated dose (up to 12 mg once weekly) as maintenance
dosage.n: Dose reduction or slower escalation for intolerable GI effects

dosage.d: Resume at the same dose if interruption is brief; re-titrate from a lower dose after prolonged interruption or intolerable GI effects
dosage.n: No labeled missed-dose window; follow trial protocol or supervising clinician direction

admin: For subcutaneous use only; inject into the abdomen or thigh and rotate injection sites
Administer once weekly on the same day each week, with or without food, per trial dosing schedules
Use only as supplied in single-dose pens, syringes, or vials; inspect for particles or discoloration before use
Hospital or clinic supervision for initiation and titration is advised given GI tolerability and investigational status
moa: Retatrutide is a single peptide triple agonist at the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and glucagon receptors, with greatest potency at GIP and lower potency at GLP-1 and glucagon receptors relative to native hormones. GIP and GLP-1 agonism enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon in hyperglycemia, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite and food intake. Added glucagon receptor agonism increases energy expenditure and hepatic fat mobilization, contributing to greater weight reduction than GLP-1-based therapy alone.

absolute: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Prior serious hypersensitivity reaction to retatrutide or any excipient
relative: Severe gastroparesis (use not recommended by class)
Diabetic retinopathy (rapid glucose improvement may transiently worsen it)
Concomitant insulin or insulin secretagogues (hypoglycemia risk)
monitor: Symptoms of MTC (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnea, persistent hoarseness)
Signs of pancreatitis and gallbladder disease
Renal function during significant GI adverse reactions with volume depletion
Heart rate and glycemic control, especially with insulin or secretagogues

preg: There are no adequate data on retatrutide use in pregnancy. Animal reproduction studies with GLP-1-based agents show embryofetal harm. Retatrutide is expected to harm the fetus and should not be used in pregnancy. Given the approximately 6-day half-life, discontinue well before a planned pregnancy (at least 2 months by class standard) and use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: There are no data on retatrutide in human milk or its effects on the infant or milk production. Because of potential serious adverse reactions and the class concern, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No labeled dose adjustment in renal impairment. Monitor renal function when initiating or escalating therapy in patients with significant nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that could cause volume depletion and acute kidney injury.
hepatic: No labeled dose adjustment; not studied in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor tolerability and glycemic control.

major: Insulin and insulin secretagogues such as sulfonylureas (increased hypoglycemia risk; reduce the concomitant agent dose)
moderate: Oral medications in general, especially narrow therapeutic index drugs (delayed gastric emptying may alter absorption; monitor)
Levothyroxine and other thyroid hormones (class-level absorption changes reported with GLP-1 agents; monitor thyroid function)
minor: No established clinically significant interactions with metformin or oral contraceptives beyond class-level absorption delay
interactions.food: May be given with or without food; delayed gastric emptying may alter absorption of concomitant oral drugs
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on hypoglycemia risk if combined with insulin or secretagogues and on added GI upset
interactions.diagnostics: Routine serum calcitonin or thyroid ultrasound screening for MTC is of uncertain value; counsel on symptoms instead

serious: Thyroid C-cell tumors / medullary thyroid carcinoma risk (class boxed warning; rodent finding, human risk unknown)
Acute kidney injury from volume depletion
rare: Thyroid C-cell tumors / medullary thyroid carcinoma (rodent finding; human risk unknown)
Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation
emergency: Anaphylaxis or angioedema - stop drug and seek emergency care
Severe persistent abdominal pain radiating to the back (possible pancreatitis) - seek urgent evaluation
Signs of dehydration with inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, or reduced urination

monitoring: Body weight, HbA1c, and fasting glucose
Signs and symptoms of thyroid tumors (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnea, persistent hoarseness)
Signs of pancreatitis and gallbladder disease
Renal function during dose escalation or significant GI losses
Heart rate, hydration status, and hypoglycemia signs when combined with insulin or secretagogues
counsel: Report a lump in the neck, trouble swallowing, shortness of breath, or persistent hoarseness (possible thyroid tumor symptoms)
Seek care for severe ongoing abdominal pain that may radiate to the back (possible pancreatitis), or right upper abdominal pain with fever (possible gallbladder disease)
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation are most common during dose escalation and usually improve; stay hydrated and report inability to keep fluids down
Tell anesthesia and surgical teams you take retatrutide before any procedure with sedation because it slows stomach emptying
Use effective contraception and discuss stopping well before a planned pregnancy given the long half-life; report hypersensitivity signs such as rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty
pk: Appetite and glycemic effects within days; weight loss accrues over weeks with titration
Plasma peak several days after a weekly subcutaneous dose at steady state
Pharmacologic effects persist for weeks after stopping; washout spans several half-lives
Refrigerate per investigational labeling at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: Investigational triple agonist (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon); as of early 2026 it has no FDA-approved dose or indication - trial maintenance doses reached 12 mg weekly
Phase 2 data showed up to about 24% mean weight loss at 48 weeks (12 mg) in obesity without diabetes and about 17% at 36 weeks with diabetes
Added glucagon agonism is intended to raise energy expenditure beyond appetite suppression, but adds heart-rate and glycemic vigilance
Expected class boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (rodent finding); contraindicated with personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2
Long half-life (about 6 days) means effects and washout persist for weeks; plan contraception and surgery holds accordingly
missed: Retatrutide has no labeled missed-dose guidance because it is investigational. In trials, a missed weekly dose was taken as soon as remembered if the next dose was more than 3 days away; otherwise it was skipped and the regular weekly schedule resumed. Do not double doses.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for retatrutide overdose. Expected effects include severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, and hypoglycemia (especially with insulin or secretagogues). Provide supportive care with fluids, electrolytes, and glucose monitoring over an extended period given the approximately 6-day half-life. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
